description: Set a Go module's in-tree version to an exact value — a Cobra command-line tool scaffolded by `iru-setup-go-cli` (`internal/version/version.go`: `var Version = "0.1.0-dev"`, overridden at release time with `-ldflags -X <module>/internal/version.Version=…`) or any Go project that keeps a `var`/`const Version = "…"` string literal in a non-test, non-generated `.go` file (including a `var (…)` block or `package main`). Follows this catalog's `x.y.z-dev` development-version convention (Step 5). Uses an embedded, tested Python helper with `--list` and `--dry-run` modes that finds every literal, refuses to write when they disagree until the user confirms, flags a `const Version` (which `-ldflags -X` silently can't override), checks every `-X …Version=` reference in `.goreleaser.yaml`, `Makefile`, `Taskfile.yml`, `justfile` and GitHub workflows against the real import path (a wrong path is silently ignored by the linker), and warns when a major version ≥ 2 doesn't match a `/vN` module-path suffix (Go's semantic import versioning — never rewritten here, it's a breaking import-path change). Reminds that for module consumers (`go get`, `go install …@vX.Y.Z`) the git tag `vX.Y.Z` is the version, so a library with no literal is reported as "version comes from git tags" and nothing is changed. Invoke as `/iru-go-bump-version <new-version>` where `<new-version>` is the literal target without a `v` (e.g. `1.4.0` or `1.5.0-dev`) — this skill never computes a bump itself (`iru-release` computes the release/next-dev values per Step 5 and passes each one through). Also accepts `args` (`key: value` lines): `sync-files: yes|no` (default: ask) to also update README/Antora version mentions, `next-version: <upcoming-version>` so that sync maps "Latest release" markers to `<new-version>` and "Current development version" markers to the upcoming value, `files: <comma list>` to restrict the search to specific `.go` files, and `dry-run: yes|no` (default `no`) to print the diff without writing anything. Reports every location found with its old value, the new value, every `-ldflags -X` reference and whether it matches, and every file touched. Use whenever the user, or `iru-release` (key `go`), needs a Go project's version set to a specific value instead of hand-editing version.go.
